newsitem.title: USA: Clinton widens lead again in CNN poll.
newsitem.headline: Clinton widens lead again in CNN poll.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton's lead in the daily CNN/USA Today tracking poll widened again on Sunday to 14 points after briefly narrowing to single digits Saturday.

The latest poll, conducted for the news organisations by the Gallup organisation Sept. 26 to Sept. 28, showed Clinton winning 51 percent of the vote, with Republican Bob Dole trailing with 37 percent and Texas billionaire Ross Perot in third place with six percent.

In the poll released Saturday, Dole had the support of 39 percent of the people surveyed, nine percentage points behind Clinton's 48 percent, CNN said. Texas billionaire Ross Perot was trailing in third place with six percent.
It was the first time the CNN tracking poll had shown Clinton with only a single digit lead.
The national poll of likely voters was conducted by Gallup and had a margin of error of plus or minus four percent.
Last week, the CNN/USA Today tracking poll put Clinton at 54 percent against 34 percent for Dole, a gap of 20 points, CNN said.
